title: Performance, Kinetics and Correlation Study of a Plug Flow Multimedia Reactor Treating Conventional UASB Effluent
content:
Three models such as Stover Kincannon, Grau, and Monod models were used to assess the kinetic coefficients for the removal of NH4–N, COD, and PO4–P in the PFMMR. The Monad model was identified as the most appropriate for characterizing the instantaneous elimination of NH4–N, COD, and PO4–P in the PFMMR.


ABSTRACT

The present study aimed to remove nutrients from anaerobically treated effluents using a plug flow multimedia reactor (PFMMR). An Up-flow Anaerobic Sludge Blanket Reactor (UASB) was used for sewage treatment. This study was conducted for 105 days to investigate the removal of NH4–N and PO4–P from the UASB effluent treating sewage through denitrification using a plastic carrier and activated carbon as a medium in the PFMMR. The results indicated that the removal efficiencies of NH4–N and PO4–P reached 91.2% and 31.0%, respectively. Correlation analysis revealed that the most robust positive correlations were between UASB and PFMMR COD effluents (0.614) and between sewage and UASB NH4-N (0.657), signifying consistent treatment behaviors for these parameters. The “Stover–Kincannon” Grau and Monod models were used to assess the kinetic coefficients for the removal of NH4–N, COD, and PO4–P in the PFMMR. The results revealed that the Monod model was the most appropriate and applicable for assessing nutrient concentrations. The PFMMR system was able to remove COD, NH4–N, and PO4–P with high removal efficiency, as shown by the low U max and high K d values. In addition, the specific growth of biomass cultivation on the multimedia was characterized by Fourier Transform Infra-red (FTIR), Dynamic light scattering (DLS), and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) methods.
